item.text: {"question_id":"5B.8","answer":"The 2023 record shows distribution-oriented policy design but does not establish fair actual incidence. PDL-145T was initiated to reduce poverty and spatial inequality through rural health centers, primary schools, and administrative buildings, but the evidence reports planned financing and delivery rather than verified execution or outcomes (BATCH-0008-E010). A September 2023 carbon-credit order allocated the state share among the Treasury, provinces, decentralized entities, and an environmental fund, with a required future evaluation; it likewise does not show disbursement or community incidence (BATCH-0024-E006). Education and girls’ empowerment measures were targeted toward vulnerable populations and low-enrollment provinces, while free education was associated with increased enrollment in 2021–2022, but these are partly pre-2023 and do not demonstrate equitable completion, quality, or benefits (BATCH-0014-E004; BATCH-0026-E009). Tshisekedi acknowledged in 2023 that purchasing-power gains and increased revenue collection had not sufficiently reached poorer people, while attributing constraints partly to global conditions and insecurity (BATCH-0015-E004). Independent 2023 evidence reports that more than 25 million people faced acute food insecurity, with conflict and inadequate rural-development investment disrupting livelihoods and disproportionately affecting conflict-affected regions (BATCH-0020-E009). Labor protections and regional minimum wages existed, but enforcement was ineffective, rural workplaces were almost never inspected, more than 97 percent of workers were reportedly informal, and marginalized groups—including Indigenous people, persons with disabilities, and women—continued to face substantial exclusion from services, employment, and effective remedies (BATCH-0011-E015). Mining-related evictions and inadequate compensation further show adverse incidence for affected communities, although the documented abuses largely predated 2023 and do not establish Tshisekedi’s personal direction (BATCH-0010-E018). The record therefore supports inclusion-oriented policies and some implementation activity, but actual distribution across classes, regions, genders, and groups remained demonstrably unequal, with attribution and 2023 incidence incompletely measured.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0024-E006","BATCH-0014-E004","BATCH-0026-E009","BATCH-0015-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0020-E009","BATCH-0011-E015","BATCH-0010-E018","BATCH-0022-E005","BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0028-E020"],"limitations_and_gaps":["There is no comprehensive 2023 incidence dataset for taxes, wages, benefits, regional investment, household consumption, or gender- and group-specific gains and burdens.","Several favorable items concern announced or planned programs, allocations, or pre-2023 outcomes rather than independently verified 2023 distributional results.","Some adverse outcomes reflect conflict, structural deprivation, inherited conditions, or private and subnational conduct; they do not by themselves establish Tshisekedi’s personal causal responsibility.","Health-financing mechanisms associated with the universal-coverage agenda lack 2023 collection, coverage, expenditure, and household-incidence results (BATCH-0020-E006)."],"corrections_made":["Removed the 2022 poverty rate and 2021–2022 enrollment comparison as direct 2023 incidence evidence; retained them only with explicit period qualification.","Recast PDL-145T, carbon-credit allocations, and girls’ education measures as policy design or planned implementation rather than proof of actual fair incidence.","Added omitted contrary evidence on currency and poverty deterioration across the tenure, informal and weakly enforced labor markets, official budget and teacher-pay claims without incidence verification, and the absence of 2023 health-financing results.","Preserved the mining-abuse evidence while narrowing its period and ruler-attribution implications."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
